<p>Borrowed-discipline-from-Paperclip — what we explicitly refuse to be:</p>

      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Not</th><th>Why</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><strong>Not opinionated about the org structure of installs</strong></td><td>"Company with CEO and reports" is one valid shape. Pipelines, swarms, tournaments, single-agent loops are other valid shapes. Plugins decide.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Not a chatbot framework</strong></td><td>Roles have jobs, not chat windows. Conversational interfaces can ship as plugins on top.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Not tied to a specific LLM provider</strong></td><td>Reference runtime uses Claude. Spec is provider-agnostic; adapters can swap.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Not an agent framework in the build-an-agent sense</strong></td><td>Agents are just role prompts + the harness contract. We don't ship an "agent class hierarchy" — that's per-install.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Not a workflow builder (no DAGs)</strong></td><td>Orchestrator decisions are dynamic; static DAGs are the failure mode we're avoiding.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Not opinionated about the domain</strong></td><td>Coding, marketing, research, ops, support — same substrate. The harness contract doesn't care.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
